bc_split_tip.blurb: Split Tip is a small cluster of boulders in the Goldfinger Sector of Hunter Creek Bouldering, in the Fraser Valley of British Columbia, at low elevation near the river. It has five problems, running from an easy V0 traverse up to V3, and most of them sit at V3. The sector is among the first boulders you meet after stepping into the trees from the forest road, which makes this a handy stop for a warm-up or a short session. Landings are the usual forest kind, so bring pads.

bc_mr_k.blurb: Mr. K is a single pyramid-shaped boulder in the Warm Up Sector of Hunter Creek Bouldering, Fraser Valley, British Columbia. The faces are tall and low in angle, with small crimps for the hands, and the landings are on the questionable side, so spotters and extra pads are worth bringing. Five problems cover a wide spread: one gentle V1, then a cluster of V4 lines and a pair that reach V5 and V6. It is a better stop for climbers who already boulder around V4 than for beginners.

bc_onions_boulder.blurb: Onions Boulder is one of five boulder groups in the Upper Right Stacks, part of The Stacks in the Fraser Valley, British Columbia. The Stacks is a cluster of boulders sitting below a wall, with the first blocks only a short walk from the car. This boulder holds five problems: three at V4, one at V5 and a single hard line at V7. That makes it a good fit for climbers who have moved past the lower grades and want steady V4 volume with one stiff project nearby.

bc_treplanning_boulder.blurb: Treplanning Boulder is one of four boulder groups in the Upper Left Stacks, within The Stacks in the Fraser Valley of British Columbia. The Stacks is a collection of boulders below a wall, with the first ones a short stroll from the parking. Five problems are here and the grades are spread out: an easy V0, a V3, two at V6 and one at V7. Most of the quality sits at the hard end, so it suits strong boulderers, although the lower-grade lines give a gentler way in.

bc_boreal_boulder.blurb: Boreal Boulder is a big, hard-to-miss block in the Lower Right Stacks, part of The Stacks in the Fraser Valley of British Columbia. It stands beside the main footpath once you pass the Chamber boulder. The five problems here include one V3, three at V4 and a single line near the top of the scale. Some lines are tall enough to feel like highballs, so pads and a spotter matter. The Stacks as a whole is a boulder cluster below a wall, reached with a short walk from the car.

bc_3rd_tier_boulders.blurb: The 3rd Tier Boulders belong to the Lemurs, a bouldering zone at Silver Lake in the Fraser Valley of British Columbia. The group begins at a cave problem and continues across the boulders as far as the last one on the upper side. It has five problems, and the grades lean hard: one mellow line around V1 or V2, then a V6, a V7 and two V8s. Strong boulderers will find the most here, while newer climbers will mostly use it as a warm-up spot before heading to other Lemurs blocks.
